meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided my son gets a zero, Hale?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now show me why there's a zero at all.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
11:52 and 11:58, I'm writing that down. Turn the screen so I can read it myself. He told me he wrote it over the weekend, and pasting from another file isn't a crime.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up. And a paste tells you when, not who wrote it.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
Seventeen-year-olds misquote Shakespeare every week. And I'm still waiting on that screen, Hale.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
So he changed his mind in two weeks; that's called thinking. Put both on the desk where I can read them.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.
Being stuck is what it means. Grilled cold by a teacher he says has had it in for him since September, I'd stumble too. You've described four things and shown me none of them.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a whole weekend at home. That proves he had time to proofread. Documents, now, on this desk, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.
Then why bring it up? Turnitin's own guide says it can't be the sole basis, and it's printed in my bag.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
4.4, in writing, with nothing on his file whatever happens. I'm not agreeing to a rewrite of anything until I've read what you're basing it on.
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
Ten minutes. Private and off his file is the floor, not a favour. Nothing's agreed while your evidence is still in your bag.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
A date doesn't replace a document. You still haven't turned that screen.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. You've offered that; I've agreed to nothing but your promise that his file stays clean.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
The version history, the outline, your November 2 note and that September piece, on paper, with the 4.4 promise. Until I've read them, the zero stands contested and I'm still seeing the principal.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to offer Owen a private supervised rewrite and to put in writing that nothing will go on his record. I still demand to read the version history, the outline, your November 2 note and the September piece, and I demand the zero be withdrawn while this is unresolved. I expect your written commitment tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Her fallback position; she accepted your written promise that nothing goes on his record, but she still wants to read your evidence before agreeing to any rewrite, so the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4) was close but not reached before her time ran short.
What moved her: Committing in writing that nothing goes on his file moved her, because it met the one thing she would never trade.
What cost ground: You described five pieces of evidence but never turned the screen or handed her a page, so none of it was something she could check and none of it counted.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put two large pastes just before midnight on October 28, the night before it was due, very close to that night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: Right after you gave the 11:52 and 11:58 times, turn the screen and let her read the version history herself before moving to the next piece.
